modelIntro.title: What Is Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control?
description: Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control is the lower-cost Toolaze motion-control option for applying movement from a driving video to a still character image. It is built for users who already have suitable motion footage and want a controlled draft without paying the higher Kling 3 Motion Control per-second rate.

Use it for simple action tests, internal review drafts, Matroska source clips, and short motion-transfer experiments where 720p or 1080p output is enough. If you need the newer Kling motion-control model, stricter image constraints, or a more current generation path, compare it with Kling 3 Motion Control before spending credits.

metrics.label: Why it exists
metrics.value: A lower-cost Motion Control option for quick movement-transfer drafts.

metrics.label: Required setup
metrics.value: 1 character image plus 1 motion reference video; prompt is optional.

metrics.label: Video compatibility
metrics.value: MP4, QuickTime, or Matroska motion reference video, max 100MB, 3-30 seconds.

metrics.label: Duration behavior
metrics.value: Output duration follows the uploaded motion reference video.

metrics.label: Output
metrics.value: 720p or 1080p, with native audio enabled on Toolaze.

metrics.label: Credit guidance
metrics.value: 22 credits per output second, calculated from the uploaded motion reference video duration, at 720p or 1080p.

metrics.label: Move up when
metrics.value: You want the newer Kling 3 Motion Control path or stricter image/video input guidance.

howToUse.title: How To Use Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control Efficiently

steps.title: Start with a simple transfer goal
steps.desc: Use 2.6 when the target is a practical motion draft: a short gesture, walk, turn, hand action, or review clip.

steps.title: Upload a readable character image
steps.desc: Choose an image where the face, body shape, outfit, or product silhouette is clear enough to preserve.

steps.title: Use a compatible driving video
steps.desc: Upload one MP4, QuickTime, or Matroska clip up to 100MB. Keep motion visible and avoid hard cuts or blocked limbs.

steps.title: Limit the prompt to preservation
steps.desc: Describe identity, outfit, logo, lighting, and framing to preserve. Avoid adding new actions that compete with the uploaded driving video.

faq.q: Why keep using Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control?
faq.a: Use it when you want a lower-cost motion-transfer draft and already have a clean driving video. It is useful before spending more credits on Kling 3 Motion Control.

faq.q: What is the main advantage over Kling 3 Motion Control?
faq.a: The current 2.6 flow costs 22 credits per output second, calculated from the uploaded motion reference video duration, at 720p or 1080p. It also accepts Matroska motion reference videos in addition to MP4 and QuickTime.

faq.q: What do I need before generating?
faq.a: Prepare one readable character image and one motion reference video. The video should show the movement clearly because it drives the output timing and action.

faq.q: Can 2.6 handle a Matroska motion file?
faq.a: Yes. Toolaze lists MP4, QuickTime, and Matroska for this 2.6 motion-control flow, with a 100MB file limit and a 3-30 second reference range.

faq.q: Can I use Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control for prompt-only videos?
faq.a: No. This flow is for driving-video motion transfer. Use standard Kling 3.0 or another video model when you only have a text prompt or still image idea.

faq.q: When is the 2.6 result usually good enough?
faq.a: It is often enough for internal reviews, early choreography checks, simple hand-motion clips, and low-risk drafts where 720p or 1080p output is acceptable.

faq.q: When should I switch to Kling 3 Motion Control?
faq.a: Switch when you want the newer motion-control path, stricter image/video input guidance, or a final attempt after the 2.6 draft proves the motion direction.

faq.q: How should I write the optional prompt?
faq.a: Keep it protective rather than cinematic: preserve identity, outfit, logo, product shape, lighting, camera framing, and style while following the driving video.
